name: Goblin
summary: Across Azeroth, goblins bargain, build, and trade for profit. Their cartels began on the Isle of Kezan, and their craft and hunger for gain now reach far beyond it. Most keep neutral so they can trade with both Alliance and Horde, while the Venture Company and Steamwheedle Cartel leave their mark across the world.

sections.title: Cartels of Kezan
sections.body: Goblins come from the Isle of Kezan in the South Seas. Long ago, rival economic cartels divided their society. Their leaders sought profit through hard bargaining, volatile engineering, and industry. They built neither kingdoms nor armies, and their ventures now reach across the world.

sections.title: Mercenaries and Mercantilism
sections.body:
During the Second War, Trade Prince Steamwheedle joined his cartel to Orgrim Doomhammer's Horde. Goblins supplied maps, siege craft, and knowledge of fleet-building in return for plunder taken from Stormwind. After the Horde fell, the cartels learned that open allegiance cost them profitable markets.

Today, the major cartels claim neutrality and keep trade havens such as Booty Bay in Stranglethorn Vale and Gadgetzan in the Tanaris desert. Alliance and Horde travelers meet there without drawn blades, while port bruisers keep the peace.

sections.title: Hired Hands and Industry
sections.body:
For many goblins, gold comes before every other loyalty. Some serve beyond the neutral cartels as hired specialists or ruthless industrial barons. The Venture Company cuts forests and strips resources across continents, heedless of local people.

In the Deadmines, goblin engineers Sneed, Gilnid, and Captain Greenskin serve criminal enterprises. They oversee smelters and shipwrights building a massive ironclad juggernaut for the Defias Brotherhood.

faq.q: Are goblins aligned with the Alliance or the Horde?
faq.answer: Neither. The major trade cartels, including the Steamwheedle Cartel, claim neutrality so they can trade with both sides. Individual goblins and private firms sell their services to the Horde, Alliance, or groups such as the Defias Brotherhood for the right price.

faq.q: Why are goblin inventions so prone to exploding?
aliases: why do goblin machines blow up
faq.answer: Goblin engineers favor raw power, speed, cheap production, and strong explosive force over structural safety. Their devices can bring spectacular results and blasts in equal measure.

The Steamwheedle Cartel is the mainland's most influential trading cartel. It runs important neutral ports and routes between continents, including Booty Bay in southern Stranglethorn and Gadgetzan in the Tanaris desert.

The Venture Company is a ruthless goblin-run industrial power known for cutting forests, strip-mining, and extracting oil. It pays little heed to local law or the land's balance, and often clashes violently with native peoples.

faq.q: Why are there goblins working with the Defias in the Deadmines?
faq.answer: The Defias Brotherhood had plenty of plundered coin and raw ore from the Moonbrook mines, so it could hire skilled goblin specialists. Sneed, Gilnid, and Captain Greenskin took contracts to oversee heavy smelting and build Edwin VanCleef's ironclad juggernaut.
Goblins come from the Isle of Kezan in the South Seas. Their great trading cartels first rose there, building an empire of commerce and industrial smog.

angles.text: As an engineer, you can favor explosive force, offensive gadgets, and risky mechanical devices. Gnomes favor precise, defensive designs.
As a miner, you help fuel goblin industry and trade. Goblin cartels fiercely guard valuable mineral claims across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms.
As an Alliance member, you may distrust goblin neutrality. The cartels once served the Old Horde as mercenaries, supplying warships and sappers during the Second War.
As a member of Thrall's Horde, you can use goblin mechanics and trade through neutral hubs. The mercenary contracts between Orgrim Doomhammer and Trade Prince Steamwheedle remain fresh in memory.
